title: Program for sum of n natural numbers - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Given a positive integer n, find the sum of the first n natural numbers.

Examples : 

Input: n = 3
Output: 6
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6

Input: n = 5
Output: 15
Explanation: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15

Try It Yourself

Table of Content

  • [Naive Approach] Loop - O(n) Time and O(1) Space
  • [Better Approach] Recursion -O(n) and O(n) Space
  • [Expected Approach] Formula Based Method- O(1) Time and O(1) Space

Sum of Natural Numbers is represented by Triangular Numbers.

[Naive Approach] Loop - O(n) Time and O(1) Space

The idea is to initialize sum to 0 and iterate from 1 to n, adding each number to sum. After the loop ends, return sum.

Consider n = 4

  • Initially : sum = 0
  • i = 1, sum = sum + 1 = 1
  • i = 2, sum = sum + 2 = 3
  • i = 3, sum = sum + 3 = 6
  • i = 4, sum = sum + 4 = 10
C++ 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int findSum(int n){
    int sum = 0;
    
    // iterating over all the numbers 
    // between 1 to n
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)
    {
        sum = sum + i;
    }
    return sum;
}
int main()
{
    int n = 5;
    cout << findSum(n);
    return 0;
}

[Better Approach] Recursion -O(n) and O(n) Space

We use recursion to find the sum of the first n natural numbers.

  • The function calls itself with (n-1) until it reaches the base case of n = 1.
  • Each call adds the current value of n to the sum of smaller values.
C++ 
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int findSum (int  n){
    
    // base condition
    if (n == 1 )
     return  1 ;
    return n + findSum(n - 1); 
}
int main() {
    int n = 5 ;
    cout <<  findSum(n); 
    return 0;
}
Java 
public class GFG {

        return n + findSum(n - 1);
    }

        int n = 5;
        System.out.println(findSum(n));
    }
}

[Expected Approach] Formula Based Method- O(1) Time and O(1) Space

The sum of the first n natural numbers can be calculated directly using the formula: (n * (n+1)) / 2

We can prove this formula using mathematical induction.

Base Case:

  • For n = 1,
  • Sum = 1 * (1 + 1) / 2 = 1
  • Thus, the formula holds for (n = 1).

Induction Hypothesis:

  • Assume the formula is true for n = k, i.e.,
  • Sum of first k numbers = k * (k + 1) / 2

Induction Step:

  • Putting k = n - 1, we get
  • Sum of first n - 1 numbers = (n - 1) * n / 2
  • If we add n to this sum, we get,

Sum of first n numbers = n + (n - 1) * n / 2

= (2n + n2 - n) / 2

= n * (n + 1) / 2

Hence, the formula is proved.
